claim.pdf_says: (page 20, folio xii, ends after the table of contents line "INDEX ... XVIII-1" and the folio "xii"; the heading "SECTION I:  INTRODUCTORY INFORMATION" is printed only on page 21, folio I-1)
claim.why_it_matters: A stray level-1 heading follows the folio of page 20, duplicating the section heading that page 21 carries (as "## <u>SECTION I: INTRODUCTORY INFORMATION</u>"). Page 20 prints no such heading; the document now has two SECTION I headings at different levels, one under the wrong page.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 20 shows the table of contents continuing from Chapter 2 (2.1, 2.2), APPENDIX C chapters 1-4, INDEX ... XVIII-1, then blank space, the folio 'xii' and the INCITS license line. No 'SECTION I: INTRODUCTORY INFORMATION' heading is printed anywhere on the page. The markdown for page 20 ends with 'xii' followed by '# SECTION I: INTRODUCTORY INFORMATION', and page 21's markdown separately carries '## <u>SECTION I: INTRODUCTORY INFORMATION</u>' after the standard's title lines. So the transcription holds a duplicate SECTION I heading at a different level, placed under page 20. The heading is not furniture, wrapping or reflow of anything on page 20; it is added text that creates a spurious section boundary in the document's heading structure. The claim quotes both sources accurately. Its effect is structural, not normative: no rule text changes.
